I can't rule out around the edge to (4,1) or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: around the edge to (4,1).
I can't rule out right, down or up yet, so I'll make an educated guess: right.
Going up would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes down.
Going left would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes right.
Going up, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (4,4); going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes right.
The line must go up: right is number 11, which comes later; down is number 15, which comes later.
Cell (4,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Number 5 is only reachable this way.
Number 6 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going right would force the line onto number 10 before its turn. So the line goes up.
Number 7 is only reachable this way.
The line must go left: around the edge to (6,2) is number 14, which comes later.
Going around the edge to (6,1) would leave both cell (5,1) and number 14 needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes down.
Cell (3,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes around the edge to (3,6).
Going left would leave both number 10 and cell (4,5) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes up.
The line must go left: up is number 16, which comes later.
Going down would leave both number 10 and cell (4,5) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going up, the next 6 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 11. So the line goes left.
Going up would strand number 10: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Going around the edge to (1,5) would leave number 13 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes right.
Going around the edge to (6,1) would leave both cell (5,1) and number 14 needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes around the edge to (5,1).
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
